findings.title: CallbackMatrixKotlinTest completeness check depends on test order and sibling success
findings.description: Test 'z every CALLBACK_TYPES interface was exercised' compares the static 'exercised' set, which is filled only by the other five tests of the class (relies on @FixMethodOrder NAME_ASCENDING). Run alone or with a --tests filter it fails with a misleading set difference, and when any earlier test fails it adds a second, derived failure that hides which interface was not reached.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the completeness check independent: assert inside each test (or in an @AfterClass) only for the interfaces that test owns, or have each test return the set of hit() names and compare their union in one test that calls them itself.

findings.title: KotlinSurfaceKotlinTest never runs the WebSocketSession call it claims to exercise
findings.description: FR-KT-002 AC-3 asks for a Kotlin call of one method of WebSocketSession. The test only registers app.ws("/ws") { _, ws -> ws.onText { ... } }; no WebSocket session is opened, so the lambda holding ws.onText/ws.sendText is compiled but never executed. The check is compile-only for that type, unlike the other four types, and the test name says the types are used without a backtick.
findings.suggested_fix: Open a session through InMemoryHttpAdapter (as CallbackMatrixKotlinTest does) and assert the echoed frame, or state in the test that WebSocketSession is covered at compile time only.

findings.title: Docs tests locate files through user.dir-relative paths and one exact-indent source literal
findings.description: KotlinAccessorTable.rows (line 24), NullableAccessorDocsTest.kotlinSource (22-23), KotlinDocsMarkersTest.root (25-27) and the negative test at KotlinDocsExamplesKotlinTest 783-787 read docs/api and test sources from System.getProperty("user.dir") plus '../' or a module-relative path, so they work only when the test JVM starts in the module directory (Gradle default; IDE or a changed workingDir breaks them). The negative test also asserts source.contains of a line with exactly 12 leading spaces, so a pure reformat of the kotlin.md#4 test fails it with an unrelated assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Pass the repository root and module directory as system properties from build.gradle (like naruserve.apiJar) and build paths from them; match the removed line after whitespace normalisation instead of an exact-indent literal.

findings.title: Marker check accepts trivial block lines and an unconstrained adapted comment
findings.description: missingLine returns null (block fully accepted) as soon as any '// adapted: <text>' line sits in the extent (line 107), with no check of the reason; 9 of the 47 blocks use it. For the others a block line only has to equal some extent line in any order, so lines such as '}' or '})' match anything and a block can lose its substance without a failure. The extent of the last marker of a file also runs to the end of the source.
findings.suggested_fix: Ignore pure-brace lines when computing the missing set, require each adapted block to still match at least its first non-trivial line, and end an extent at the next top-level @Test/fun boundary.
